issues.display_title: Issue #544: Hardening Unsafe Type Assertions in PostsHandlers
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Hardening Unsafe Type Assertions in PostsHandlers

Summary

Hardened all unsafe type assertions and unmarshaling access points in src/Controllers/V1/Posts/PostsHandlers.go:

  1. Protected Payload Extraction (UploadPanoramaPostV1):

    • Added validation check !okData || dataStr == "" preventing empty payload publishing to RabbitMQ.

  2. Hardened Type Assertions (AddPostCompleteV1):

    • defaultSettings & isPost: Replaced direct type casting with safe assertion okDefault and empty checks, returning 400 Bad Request ("Required Body") instead of panicking when default is nil or not a JSON map.
    • action: Added safe string assertion and fallback to "draft".
    • multiple: Added safe slice assertion okMultiples ensuring multiples is a valid slice with len > 0.
    • panorama: Added parsePanoramaDefault helper to safely parse float64, float32, int, and int64 representations without type-assertion panics.
    • u_name: Added safe slice assertion okUNames before calculating bounds check panoramaDefault > float64(len(uNames)).
    • lastLogin & userId: Guarded extraction from userDatas map with safe string assertions.

  3. Guarded Database Nil Checks in Error Logging & Cache:

    • In src/Utils/Functions/response.go (SaveLogErr): Added guard if Config.DB == nil { return nil } preventing nil pointer panics during uninitialized database states.
    • In src/Utils/Redis/user_cache.go (ReplaceUserDetails): Added guard if Config.DB == nil { return "User Not Found" }.

  4. Created Automated Tests:

    • Created src/Controllers/V1/Posts/PostsHandlers_test.go covering:
      • TestParsePanoramaDefault: Verifying float, int, string, and nil inputs.
      • TestUploadPanoramaPostV1_InvalidJSON: Verifying invalid JSON rejection.
      • TestUploadPanoramaPostV1_EmptyData: Verifying empty data rejection.
      • TestAddPostCompleteV1_InvalidJSON: Verifying invalid body rejection.
      • TestAddPostCompleteV1_EmptyData: Verifying empty data rejection.
      • TestAddPostCompleteV1_InvalidBase64: Verifying malformed base64 rejection.
      • TestAddPostCompleteV1_InvalidInnerJSON: Verifying inner payload JSON rejection.
      • TestAddPostCompleteV1_MissingDefaultDoesNotPanic: Verifying that missing/nil default object returns a clean error response without panicking.

Files Updated

1. Controllers

  • src/Controllers/V1/Posts/PostsHandlers.go:
    • Added parsePanoramaDefault(val interface{}) (float64, bool).
    • Added guards for dataStr, defaultSettings, isPost, action, multiples, panoramaDefault, uNames, and userDatas.
  • src/Controllers/V1/Posts/PostsHandlers_test.go:
    • 8 unit tests validating error envelopes and panic immunity.

2. Utilities

  • src/Utils/Functions/response.go:
    • Added if Config.DB == nil { return nil } in SaveLogErr.
  • src/Utils/Redis/user_cache.go:
    • Added if Config.DB == nil { return "User Not Found" } in ReplaceUserDetails.

Verification

  • Lint / Vet:

    go vet ./...
# PASS (0 warnings / 0 errors)

  • Tests:

    go test -v ./src/Controllers/V1/Posts/...
# PASS: TestParsePanoramaDefault
# PASS: TestUploadPanoramaPostV1_InvalidJSON
# PASS: TestUploadPanoramaPostV1_EmptyData
# PASS: TestAddPostCompleteV1_InvalidJSON
# PASS: TestAddPostCompleteV1_EmptyData
# PASS: TestAddPostCompleteV1_InvalidBase64
# PASS: TestAddPostCompleteV1_InvalidInnerJSON
# PASS: TestAddPostCompleteV1_MissingDefaultDoesNotPanic

go test ./...
# PASS (all repository test suites pass)

Problem

In src/Controllers/V1/Posts/PostsHandlers.go, the handler AddPostCompleteV1 performs direct unchecked type assertions on decoded request payloads (postsData map) and user session dictionaries (userDatas map):

  1. defaultSettings := postsData["default"].(map[string]interface{}): Panics if default is nil, primitive, or omitted.
  2. isPost := postsData["is_post"].(string): Panics if is_post is nil or non-string.
  3. action := postsData["action"].(string): Panics if action is nil or non-string.
  4. multiples := postsData["multiple"].([]interface{}): Panics if multiple is nil or not a slice.
  5. panoramaDefault = defaultSettings["panorama"].(float64): Panics if panorama is nil or passed as an integer/string.
  6. postsData["u_name"].([]interface{}): Panics if u_name is nil or not a slice.
  7. userDatas["last_login"].(string) and userDatas["user_id"].(string): Panics if session values are missing or not string.

Any malformed or malicious payload targeting /v1/posts/complete triggers an unhandled Go runtime panic (panic: interface conversion: interface {} is nil, not ...), terminating the request abruptly and causing HTTP 500 crashes instead of structured 400 Bad Request validation errors.

Scope

  1. Safe Type Guarding in src/Controllers/V1/Posts/PostsHandlers.go:

    • Add two-value type assertion checks (val, ok := ...) for default, is_post, action, multiple, u_name, last_login, and user_id.
    • Add flexible numeric parsing for panorama allowing both float64, integer, and string representations.
    • Return clean 400 Bad Request responses with descriptive validation messages whenever required fields are absent or of unexpected types.

  2. Automated Unit Testing (src/Controllers/V1/Posts/PostsHandlers_test.go):

    • Test invalid JSON body.
    • Test empty base64 payload.
    • Test corrupted base64 data.
    • Test payload with missing/nil default object (ensuring no panic).
    • Test payload with missing/nil is_post string (ensuring no panic).
    • Test payload with invalid action value (ensuring no panic).
    • Test payload with missing/nil multiple slice (ensuring no panic).
    • Test payload with missing/nil u_name slice (ensuring no panic).

Behavior Boundary

  • 100% Backward Compatible:
    • Valid client requests produce the exact same responses, headers, and behavior as before.
    • Invalid client requests receive well-formed JSON error envelopes (Functions.ErrorResponse) instead of unhandled runtime panics.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Zero unchecked type assertions in PostsHandlers.go.
  • All malformed payload scenarios return standard 400 Bad Request without triggering panics.
  • go vet ./... passes cleanly with zero warnings.
  • go test ./... passes across all packages.

Delivery

issues.display_title: Issue #545: Refactor and Harden Worker PostComplete
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Refactor and Harden Worker PostComplete

Summary

Hardened src/Worker/PostComplete/PostComplete.go against crashes, double-ACK protocol bugs, unchecked type assertions, and duplicate notification logic:

  1. Panic Recovery Guard:

    • Wrapped the RabbitMQ message consumption callback in a deferred recover() block. If any unexpected payload causes a panic, the worker intercepts it, logs context via log.Printf, rejects the message with delivery.Reject(false) to prevent poison pill loops, and avoids daemon crashes.

  2. Fixed AMQP Acknowledgment Ordering:

    • Moved defer delivery.Ack(false) to execute only after base64 decoding and JSON deserialization succeed.
    • Malformed payloads are rejected immediately with _ = delivery.Reject(false).

  3. Hardened Type Assertions:

    • Replaced raw casting with safe type assertions for sid, u_name, defaultSettings, action, multiples, panoramaDefault, and hotspots.
    • Prevented panics if any nested map field is missing or malformed.

  4. Unified Push Notification Logic:

    • Replaced 75+ lines of duplicate token loading, chunking, and broadcasting with Moderation.PushUserMobileAndWeb.

  5. Ansible Deployment Update:

    • In ansible-deploy.yml, uncommented development-PostComplete with count: 1 in the worker restart loop.

Files Updated

1. Worker Daemon

  • src/Worker/PostComplete/PostComplete.go:
    • Added panic recovery handler.
    • Corrected AMQP ACK/Reject order.
    • Added safe type assertions.
    • Adopted Moderation.PushUserMobileAndWeb.

2. Deployment

  • ansible-deploy.yml:
    • Uncommented development-PostComplete with count: 1.

Verification

  • Lint / Vet:

    go vet ./...
# PASS (0 warnings / 0 errors)

  • Tests:

    go test -v ./src/Worker/PostComplete/...
# PASS (all test cases pass)

go test ./...
# PASS (all repository test suites pass)

Problem

src/Worker/PostComplete/PostComplete.go handles post finalization in the background after all panorama tiles have been uploaded. However, several critical reliability issues were identified:

  1. No Panic Recovery Guard: The AMQP consumer callback runs without a recover() handler. Unhandled panics from corrupted payloads or nil interface assertions terminate the entire worker process.
  2. Double-ACK AMQP Bug: defer delivery.Ack(false) is set before decoding base64 and unmarshaling JSON payloads. Malformed messages execute the deferred ACK instead of rejecting the invalid delivery.
  3. Unchecked Type Assertions: Field extractions (sid, u_name, default, is_post, action, multiple, panorama, and hotspot items) perform raw casting (.(string), .(map[string]interface{}), .(float64)) that trigger runtime panics on unexpected data types.
  4. Duplicate Notification Logic: Lines 758–832 manually query push_notification and notifications_web, chunk tokens, and dispatch broadcasts, duplicating code already unified in src/Utils/Moderation/.

Scope

  1. Panic Protection:

    • Add a deferred recover() block inside the consumer callback in src/Worker/PostComplete/PostComplete.go that logs the panic context and rejects the message with delivery.Reject(false).

  2. Fix AMQP Acknowledgment Order:

    • Move defer delivery.Ack(false) to execute only after base64 decoding and JSON unmarshaling succeed.
    • Reject malformed payloads immediately with _ = delivery.Reject(false).

  3. Harden Type Assertions:

    • Use two-value assertions (val, ok := ...) for all payload extraction points (sid, default, is_post, action, multiple, and hotspot map casting).

  4. Reuse Shared Notification Dispatcher:

    • Replace 75+ lines of duplicate token loading and chunking with Moderation.PushUserMobileAndWeb.

  5. Ansible Deployment:

    • Uncomment development-PostComplete with count: 1 in ansible-deploy.yml.

Behavior Boundary

  • 100% Backward Compatible:
    • Database schema, table queries, Redis triggers, Centrifugo channels, and notification contents remain completely unchanged.
  • Fail-Safe: Malformed messages never crash the worker daemon.

Acceptance Criteria

  • PostComplete recovers gracefully from runtime panics and invalid message payloads.
  • development-PostComplete is active in ansible-deploy.yml.
  • go vet ./... passes cleanly with zero warnings.
  • go test ./... passes across all packages.

Delivery

Implemented on 2026-10-12.

issues.display_title: Issue #543: Add Timeouts to Outbound HTTP Requests Across OAuth and Media Ingestion
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Add Timeouts to Outbound HTTP Requests Across OAuth and Media Ingestion

Summary

Eliminated all unbounded http.Get(...) and http.DefaultClient.Do(...) calls across OAuth authentication, avatar downloads, YouTube embed queries, and Google Maps synchronization, replacing them with HTTP clients configured with a strict 10-second deadline:

  1. Shared HTTP Client Export (src/Utils/Functions/response.go):

    • Exported Functions.HTTPClient = &http.Client{Timeout: 10 * time.Second} with connection pooling for cross-package use.

  2. OAuth Package Timeout (src/Utils/Functions/Registration/oauth.go):

    • Configured oauthHTTPClient = &http.Client{Timeout: 10 * time.Second}.
    • Replaced http.Get in VerifyGoogleToken (Google tokeninfo API) and VerifyAppleToken (Apple JWK keys endpoint) with oauthHTTPClient.Get.

  3. Avatar and Media Ingestion Handlers:

    • src/Action/V1/Register/register_helpers.go: Replaced unbounded http.Get(avatarURL) in processOAuthAvatar with Functions.HTTPClient.Get.
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/AddPost.go: Replaced 3 unbounded http.Get calls for YouTube and GVT thumbnails, as well as http.DefaultClient.Do(req) for YouTube oEmbed, with Functions.HTTPClient.
    • src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions/maps_sync.go: Replaced unbounded http.Get in SyncPostWithMapsPanorra for sync and thumbnail generation with Functions.HTTPClient.Get.
    • src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions/image_signing.go: Replaced unbounded http.Get(imageUrl) in ProcessThumbnail with Functions.HTTPClient.Get.

  4. Unit Tests:

    • Added TestOAuthHTTPClientTimeout and TestVerifyGoogleTokenInvalidToken in src/Utils/Functions/Registration/oauth_test.go.

Files Updated

1. HTTP Client & Utilities

  • src/Utils/Functions/response.go: Exported HTTPClient.
  • src/Utils/Functions/Registration/oauth.go: Added oauthHTTPClient, protected Google and Apple OAuth token requests.
  • src/Utils/Functions/Registration/oauth_test.go: Added timeout and error handling tests.

2. Media & Sync Handlers

  • src/Action/V1/Register/register_helpers.go: Replaced http.Get with Functions.HTTPClient.Get.
  • src/Action/V1/Posts/AddPost.go: Replaced http.Get and http.DefaultClient.Do with Functions.HTTPClient.
  • src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions/maps_sync.go: Replaced http.Get with Functions.HTTPClient.Get.
  • src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions/image_signing.go: Replaced http.Get with Functions.HTTPClient.Get.

Verification

  • Lint / Vet:

    go vet ./...
# PASS (0 warnings / 0 errors)

  • Tests:

    go test -v ./src/Utils/Functions/Registration/...
# PASS: TestOAuthHTTPClientTimeout
# PASS: TestVerifyGoogleTokenInvalidToken

go test -v ./src/Action/V1/Register/...
# PASS (all tests pass)

go test -v ./src/Action/V1/Posts/...
# PASS (all tests pass)

go test ./...
# PASS (all repository test suites pass)

Problem

Multiple outbound HTTP requests across registration, OAuth verification, Google/Apple authentication, and media processing use http.Get(...) directly.
In Go, http.Get(...) relies on http.DefaultClient, which has zero timeout (unbounded/infinite timeout):

  1. Google OAuth Token Verification: src/Utils/Functions/Registration/oauth.go calls http.Get("https://oauth2.googleapis.com/tokeninfo?id_token=" + ...) without a timeout.
  2. Apple OAuth JWK Fetching: src/Utils/Functions/Registration/oauth.go calls http.Get("https://appleid.apple.com/auth/keys") without a timeout.
  3. OAuth Avatar Image Ingestion: src/Action/V1/Register/register_helpers.go calls http.Get(avatarURL) without a timeout.
  4. YouTube & GVT Thumbnail Downloads: src/Action/V1/Posts/AddPost.go calls http.Get(thumbnailYT) and http.Get(thumbnailGvt) without a timeout.
  5. Maps Synchronization: src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions/maps_sync.go calls http.Get(url) and http.Get(thumbURL) without a timeout.
  6. Thumbnail URL Ingestion: src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions/image_signing.go calls http.Get(imageUrl) without a timeout.

If any external third-party API or content server is unresponsive, throttles connections, or stalls TCP handshakes, the Fiber worker goroutines hang indefinitely, causing file descriptor leaks, memory bloat, and thread pool exhaustion.

Scope

  1. Shared HTTP Client Export:

    • In src/Utils/Functions/response.go, export HTTPClient with a strict 10 * time.Second timeout and connection pool reuse (var HTTPClient = &http.Client{Timeout: 10 * time.Second}).

  2. OAuth Package Timeout:

    • In src/Utils/Functions/Registration/oauth.go, configure a dedicated oauthHTTPClient = &http.Client{Timeout: 10 * time.Second} for Google tokeninfo and Apple public keys retrieval.

  3. Media & Registration Handlers:

    • src/Action/V1/Register/register_helpers.go: Replace http.Get in processOAuthAvatar with Functions.HTTPClient.Get.
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/AddPost.go: Replace http.Get in thumbnail download sections with Functions.HTTPClient.Get.
    • src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions/maps_sync.go: Replace http.Get with Functions.HTTPClient.Get.
    • src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions/image_signing.go: Replace http.Get with Functions.HTTPClient.Get.

  4. Testing & Verification:

    • Add unit tests in src/Utils/Functions/Registration/oauth_test.go verifying client timeout configuration and error handling.
    • Run full regression test suite across the entire codebase.

Behavior Boundary

  • 100% Backward Compatible:
    • Valid requests to Google, Apple, and thumbnail services continue to operate identically.
    • Failures and timeouts return structured error logs and responses instead of hanging processes.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Zero calls to unbounded http.Get(...) in OAuth, media download, and sync paths.
  • All outbound HTTP requests enforce a maximum 10-second deadline.
  • go vet ./... passes cleanly with zero warnings.
  • go test ./... passes across all packages.

Delivery

issues.display_title: Issue #546: Refactor and Harden MentionPost and LocationGrouping Workers
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Refactor and Harden MentionPost and LocationGrouping Workers

Summary

Hardened both MentionPost and LocationGrouping background workers against unhandled panics, fixed acknowledgment timing bugs, protected unchecked type assertions, and eliminated 85+ lines of duplicate push notification code:

  1. Worker MentionPost (src/Worker/MentionPost/MentionPost.go):

    • Added deferred panic recovery guard (recover()) logging the context and dropping the message with _ = delivery.Reject(false) to prevent background daemon crashes.
    • Protected visibility field access with safe assertion visibility, _ := post["visibility"].(string).
    • Replaced 85+ lines of duplicate Expo and Web push notification token retrieval and chunking with Moderation.PushUserMobileAndWeb.
    • Removed unused "panorra-api-new/src/Models" and "panorra-api-new/src/Utils/Functions/BroadcastFunctions" imports.
    • Added unit tests in src/Worker/MentionPost/MentionPost_test.go.

  2. Worker LocationGrouping (src/Worker/LocationGrouping/LocationGrouping.go):

    • Added deferred panic recovery guard (recover()) rejecting poisoned messages with _ = delivery.Reject(false).
    • Corrected AMQP ACK timing: moved defer delivery.Ack(false) to execute only after JSON deserialization and post_id validation succeed.
    • Malformed payloads and missing post_id are rejected immediately with _ = delivery.Reject(false).
    • Added unit tests in src/Worker/LocationGrouping/LocationGrouping_test.go.

  3. Ansible Deployment (ansible-deploy.yml):

    • Per project convention, configured Restart Workers loop targeting strictly the updated workers: development-MentionPost and development-LocationGrouping with count: 1, keeping unchanged workers commented out.

Files Updated

1. Workers

  • src/Worker/MentionPost/MentionPost.go: Panic recovery, safe type assertion, adopted Moderation.PushUserMobileAndWeb.
  • src/Worker/MentionPost/MentionPost_test.go: Unit tests for unmarshaling and sid validation.
  • src/Worker/LocationGrouping/LocationGrouping.go: Panic recovery, fixed ACK/Reject order.
  • src/Worker/LocationGrouping/LocationGrouping_test.go: Unit tests for payload and post_id validation.

2. Deployment

  • ansible-deploy.yml: Configured restart loop strictly for development-MentionPost and development-LocationGrouping.

Verification

  • Lint / Vet:

    go vet ./...
# PASS (0 warnings / 0 errors)

  • Tests:

    go test -v ./src/Worker/MentionPost/... ./src/Worker/LocationGrouping/...
# PASS (all test cases pass)

go test ./src/Worker/...
# PASS (all workers pass)

go test ./...
# PASS (all repository test suites pass)

Problem

  1. Missing Panic Recovery in Workers:
    Neither src/Worker/MentionPost/MentionPost.go nor src/Worker/LocationGrouping/LocationGrouping.go wraps their AMQP message consumption callbacks with a recover() handler. Unhandled panics from unexpected payloads, malformed data, or nil pointer references cause the entire background daemon to crash and exit.

  2. Unchecked Type Assertion in MentionPost:
    In MentionPost.go, visibility := post["visibility"].(string) executes a raw type assertion on unverified query results. If visibility is null or of an unexpected type, the worker panics.

  3. Duplicated Push Notification Code in MentionPost:
    Lines 384–469 in MentionPost.go contain 85+ lines of duplicate logic querying push_notification and notifications_web, string imploding, chunking tokens (100 for mobile, 10 for web), JSON parsing, and broadcast dispatching. This exact workflow is already unified in Moderation.PushUserMobileAndWeb.

  4. Flawed AMQP Acknowledgment Order in LocationGrouping:
    LocationGrouping.go runs defer delivery.Ack(false) at the very beginning of message receipt, acknowledging malformed or empty payloads before JSON validation occurs.

Scope

  1. Harden src/Worker/MentionPost/MentionPost.go:

    • Add deferred panic recovery guard (recover()) logging errors and safely rejecting poisoned messages with _ = delivery.Reject(false).
    • Protect visibility extraction with safe type guarding (visibility, _ := post["visibility"].(string)).
    • Replace 85+ lines of duplicate mobile and web push notification dispatching with Moderation.PushUserMobileAndWeb.

  2. Harden src/Worker/LocationGrouping/LocationGrouping.go:

    • Add deferred panic recovery guard (recover()).
    • Move defer delivery.Ack(false) to execute only after JSON unmarshaling and post_id validation succeed.
    • Reject invalid JSON payloads and missing post_id with _ = delivery.Reject(false).

  3. Update Ansible Deployment (ansible-deploy.yml):

    • In accordance with the deployment convention, configure the worker restart loop to target specifically the updated workers: development-MentionPost and development-LocationGrouping with count: 1.

  4. Automated Testing:

    • Add unit tests verifying safe handling and message processing for both workers.

Behavior Boundary

  • 100% Backward Compatible:
    • Notification contents, channels, database updates, and geocoding logic remain completely unchanged.
    • Workers gracefully recover without crashing on unexpected payloads.

Acceptance Criteria

  • MentionPost and LocationGrouping recover gracefully from panics and invalid message payloads.
  • development-MentionPost and development-LocationGrouping configured in ansible-deploy.yml.
  • go vet ./... passes cleanly with zero warnings.
  • go test ./... passes across all packages.

Delivery
